subject: polity
title: Supreme Court & High Courts
description: Composition, appointment, jurisdiction, important articles — with PCJ, OAAR, OAS tricks

content.overview: The Supreme Court is the highest judicial authority in India (Article 124), while High Courts are the highest courts in each state (Article 214).
keyPoints: SUPREME COURT: Established under Article 124; seat in New Delhi
SC Composition: Chief Justice of India (CJI) + other judges; number fixed by Parliament by law (currently 34 = CJI + 33)
SC Appointment: By President after consultation with judges of SC and HCs as he deems necessary; CJI appointment — consultation with other judges mandatory

SC Jurisdiction: Original (Art 131 — Centre-State/inter-State disputes), Appellate (Art 132-136 — constitutional, civil, criminal, special leave), Advisory (Art 143), Review (Art 137); no discussion on SC conduct in Parliament (Art 121)
SC is the Guardian of the Constitution — final interpreter
HIGH COURTS: Established under Article 214; every state has one (Art 215 — HC as court of record; Arts 215-231 — related provisions)
HC Composition: Chief Justice + other judges (number fixed by President)
HC Appointment: By President after consultation with CJI, Governor of the state, and Chief Justice of that HC (for other judges)
HC Jurisdiction: Original (civil & criminal within state), Appellate (from subordinate courts), Supervisory (over all courts/tribunals in the state — Art 227)
HC Writ Powers: Article 226 — can issue writs for FRs AND for any other purpose (wider than SC's Art 32)
HC Independence: Article 217 — security of tenure; removal only by President on address by Parliament

mnemonics.explanation: SC judges are appointed by the President after Consultation with Judges of SC and HCs
SC jurisdiction: Original (131), Appellate (132-136), Advisory (143), Review (137)
Key SC articles: 124 (establishment), 131 (original), 136 (special leave), 143 (advisory), 137 (review), 121 (no discussion on judges' conduct in Parliament)
HC jurisdiction: Original (within state), Appellate (subordinate courts), Supervisory (Art 227 over all state courts)
Key HC articles: 214 (establishment), 215 (court of record), 226 (writ powers — wider than Art 32), 217 (appointment & independence of judges)

mnemonics.trick: 226 > 32 = HC writs for FRs + any other purpose; SC writs only for FRs
mnemonics.explanation: Article 226 (HC) is wider than Article 32 (SC) — HC can issue writs for FRs and 'for any other purpose'

quiz.question: Which article establishes the Supreme Court?
quiz.explanation: Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court of India

quiz.question: High Courts are established under which article?
Which article gives High Courts writ powers?
quiz.explanation: Article 226 gives High Courts writ powers — wider than Article 32 as it covers FRs and 'any other purpose'

quiz.question: The Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction is under:
quiz.explanation: Article 143 gives the Supreme Court advisory jurisdiction (President can seek SC's opinion)

quiz.question: Discussion on the conduct of SC judges in Parliament is barred by:
quiz.explanation: Article 121 bars discussion in Parliament on the conduct of SC judges (except during removal motion)

quiz.question: The supervisory jurisdiction of High Courts over subordinate courts is under:
quiz.explanation: Article 227 gives High Courts supervisory jurisdiction over all courts and tribunals in the state

timeline.event: Supreme Court of India inaugurated (28 Jan 1950)
